clue.text: Disturbed lad's behind, should be coaxed gently

indicators.note: something disturbed is thrown out of order, so the letters of the words that follow are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, with its S counted as a letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A troubled boy's backside needs gentle handling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbed' rearranges LADS and BEHIND together; 'should be' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To blandish is to flatter or cajole, so someone blandished has been persuaded by sweet talk.

clue.text: Shout disapproval at maiden, making loud noise

parts.note: to shout disapproval at a performer is to boo
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A crowd jeers at a young woman, raising a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, abbreviated M on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: A boom is a deep resonant sound, such as thunder or a cannon's report.

clue.text: Question from someone who doubts his capacity to be good-natured?

definitions.text: Question from someone who doubts his capacity

explanation.surface: A self-doubting person asks whether they can be kind.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into three words and it is the worried question of someone unsure of their ability.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as three words it asks whether one is capable; as one word it means friendly and pleasant.

clue.text: Protest from wicked person right inside HQ?

parts.note: a demon is an evil spirit or a cruel, wicked person

indicators.note: inside means the letter for right is placed within the word for headquarters

parts.note: a station, such as a police or military station, is a headquarters base

explanation.surface: A rally organised by a villain from within a command centre.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a station is only one sort of HQ.
explanation.definitionFit: A demonstration is a public march or rally held to protest.

clue.text: Term seems terrible, term never ending

indicators.note: terrible suggests something badly mangled, so the letters of seems are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: never ending means the word term loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gloomy student grumbles that the term looks dreadful and drags on forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges SEEMS to SEMES; 'never ending' cuts M from TERM, leaving TER.
explanation.definitionFit: A semester is a half-year academic period at a school or university.

clue.text: Female in charge in a particular period

indicators.note: the in after charge tells us one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: an era is a particular period of history
IC is the usual abbreviation for in charge, the officer with command

explanation.surface: A woman takes command during a certain historical age.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a woman's given name, and crosswords often define names by sex alone.

clue.text: Capture vagrant, male to be put away

indicators.note: to be put away means the letter for male is removed from the word for vagrant

parts.note: a tramp is a homeless wanderer, a vagrant

explanation.surface: Police seize a homeless man and lock him up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put away' suggests jailing, but it means the M is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To trap an animal or person is to catch and hold them.

clue.text: Perhaps it was Chris Evans who embarrassed leader

parts.note: someone embarrassed goes red in the face
a head is a leader, as of a school

explanation.surface: A celebrity is blamed for humiliating a boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Chris Evans is a ginger-haired British radio and TV presenter; 'Perhaps' flags him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The broadcaster is famous for his ginger hair, making him one example of a person with red hair.

clue.text: Movement against elaborate ritual gets antis out to block Jewish festival

indicators.note: to block means one group of letters sits inside another, stopping it up

parts.note: Purim is the Jewish festival commemorating Esther

indicators.note: out signals the letters of antis are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Protesters against ornate religious ceremony disrupt a Jewish holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals the anagram of the protesters' word, and 'to block' puts that jumble inside the festival, as a barricade stops a road. Purim is the spring feast recalling Esther.
explanation.definitionFit: Puritanism was a Protestant movement opposing ornate ceremony in worship.

clue.text: General disgust when leader leaves platform

indicators.note: leader leaves means the first letter of the word for platform departs

parts.note: a podium is a raised platform for a speaker

explanation.surface: Widespread revulsion as the chief walks off the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' is part of the definition, not a military officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is widespread hatred or contempt felt by many people.

clue.text: Way of doing business said to suit the monks?

indicators.note: said shows that the phrase is spoken and heard as a soundalike

parts.note: a monastic order is a male order, one that suits men

explanation.surface: A trading method is claimed to be ideal for a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail order is selling goods by post from a catalogue.

clue.text: Ill-advised drink taken by somebody going from saloon to saloon?

definitions.text: Ill-advised drink taken by somebody going from saloon to saloon?

parts.words: Ill-advised drink taken by somebody going from saloon to saloon?
parts.note: the last glass before leaving the saloon bar of a pub to drive off in a saloon car

explanation.surface: A pub crawler has a final unwise drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A saloon is both a smarter bar in a British pub and a family car, so the drinker goes from bar to car.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a last drink before setting off, unwise when driving.

clue.text: Piece of paper giving credit to someone financially sound?

definitions.text: Piece of paper giving credit to someone financially sound?

parts.words: Piece of paper giving credit to someone financially sound?
parts.note: a solvent person is called sound as a bank, and a document crediting them is a declaration about that soundness

explanation.surface: A certificate praising a solvent person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving credit' reads as praise but also means showing money paid in to an account.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank sends this printed record listing credits and debits on an account.

clue.text: A couple of pages to finish, sweet things in final parts of book?

parts.note: PP is the abbreviation for pages, a pair of P's
an end is a finish
ices are sweet frozen desserts

explanation.surface: A reader has two pages left and some treats to enjoy at the back of the book.
explanation.definitionFit: Appendices are supplementary sections placed at the back of a volume.

clue.text: Publicity row about film being made more attractive

indicators.note: about means the word for publicity plus the word for row go around the film's letters

parts.note: PR stands for public relations, publicity
a tier is a row, as of seats in a theatre
ET is the Spielberg film about an alien

explanation.surface: A publicity quarrel over a movie being glamourised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' reads as a quarrel but is a tier of seating.
explanation.definitionFit: Prettier is the comparative of pretty, meaning better looking.

clue.text: Country girl embraces rural dean

indicators.note: embraces means the girl's name wraps around the abbreviation

parts.note: Joan is a girl's name
RD is the abbreviation for rural dean, a Church of England cleric

explanation.surface: A country lass hugs the local clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' looks like an adjective for the girl but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Jordan is a kingdom in the Middle East.

clue.text: Extinct mammal revealed by degrees to professor?

parts.note: MAs are Master of Arts degrees
a don is a university teacher such as a professor

explanation.surface: A fossil beast is unveiled step by step to an academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by degrees' looks like 'gradually', but degrees are MAs.
explanation.definitionFit: The mastodon was an elephant-like beast of the Ice Age, now died out.

clue.text: Make beloved aim to acquire sense of music

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
an ear for music is a sense of it

explanation.surface: A musician aims to develop an appreciation for tunes.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear is to cause someone to be loved or liked.

clue.text: Moved slowly with father, weak inside, taken in hand

indicators.note: inside means the letter for weak is placed within the word for father

parts.note: dad is an informal word for father
led means guided, taken by the hand

explanation.surface: A frail father is helped along, walking slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawdling means lingering and going at a sluggish pace.

clue.text: Loud goings-on associated with society parties

parts.note: F is the musical notation forte, loud
actions are activities or goings-on

explanation.surface: Noisy behaviour at upper-class gatherings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parties' suggests social gatherings but means groups within a society.
explanation.definitionFit: Factions are dissenting groups or cliques within a larger body.

clue.text: Summarize unfashionable policy

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: Briefly describe an outmoded political approach.
explanation.definitionFit: To outline is to give the main points without detail.

clue.text: Drunk deserting town road where policeman stands guard

indicators.note: drunk suggests staggering, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunkard leaves town and wanders onto a street.
explanation.walkthrough: Downing Street is the London street where the British prime minister lives, guarded by police.
explanation.definitionFit: The prime minister's residence at Number 10 is on this famous London street with a police guard.

clue.text: Good American to show enthusiasm

explanation.surface: A fine American displays keenness.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is great zest or relish in doing something.

clue.text: Individuality evident in little son, mischief-maker

parts.note: little indicates a shortening, and S is the abbreviation for son
an elf is a mischievous sprite

explanation.surface: A naughty young boy shows his personality.
explanation.definitionFit: The self is a person's own identity and nature.

clue.text: Officer with one daughter is accommodated and settled

parts.note: COL is short for colonel, an army officer

indicators.note: is accommodated means the word is is housed within the word one

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An army officer and his daughter are housed and given a home.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonised means a territory has been occupied and populated by incomers.

clue.text: Girl given ring electrified

parts.note: O resembles a ring in shape
a live wire is electrified

explanation.surface: A young woman is handed a charged hoop.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Team's boastful manner

explanation.surface: A squad shows arrogance.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a sports team, and side also means a swaggering air of superiority.

clue.text: Tinned food? Gosh, Edward, grumble!

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like gosh
Ned is a pet form of Edward
a beef is a complaint or grumble

explanation.surface: Someone complains about canned food to Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Corned beef is salted cured beef often sold in cans.
